I am 76 years old, and I have worked this land for 55 years. My wife and I are the only ones left in the household — our children went to the city long ago. We have 21.4 mu of flat land here in Quzhou, and I know every piece of it. I am not going to try anything new at my age. I grow what I know, what the market in town will buy, and what these two old hands can still manage.

My main rotation is wheat-maize on the good flat fields — 15 mu. That system is mechanized now, so I can hire the tractor and combine, which saves my back. The other 6.4 mu I split between cotton (3.4 mu) and chili (3 mu). Those two take more hand labor, especially at harvest, but the prices have been decent and I have been growing them for decades. I know the rhythm.

For the **winter wheat**, it is already in the ground from last October. Now in early spring, I will top-dress urea at green-up, irrigate four times from the well (greening, jointing, heading, and grain filling), and spray twice — once for weeds and once for aphids or rust if I see it. I use the improved Jimai variety from the county co-op; it is reliable in our winters. I rotary-tilled before sowing last autumn to break up the maize stubble. I expect about 450 kg per mu — not a record, but steady.

For **summer maize**, I will plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan or Denghai, whatever the shop has that I know — right after the wheat comes off in June. I will direct-seed into the stubble with no tillage; there is no time to waste in June, and the machine can do it in one pass. I will side-dress nitrogen when the plants are knee-high, irrigate twice if the summer rains are short, and spray once for corn borer and once for weeds. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For **cotton**, I will rotary-till the 3.4 mu plot in April and plant the improved Guoxinmian variety. Cotton needs many sprays here for bollworm — I will spray 12 times through the season, no skipping, or the worms will ruin it. I will irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll filling, and apply compound fertilizer at planting plus a top-dressing of urea. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

For **chili** on the 3 mu near the house, I will rotary-till in late April and transplant the improved yangjiaohong seedlings. Chili needs a lot of water and fertilizer — I will irrigate five times and fertilize heavily, especially potash, or the peppers will be small. I will spray 12 times for mites and diseases. It is hard work, but 2,600 kg per mu of fresh chili pays well enough at the wholesale market to be worth the ache in my knees.
